title: A benchmark result row carries no environment fingerprint, so a score cannot be reproduced or compared with the one it is plotted against
problem: Our agent scores 4 points lower than the paper reported and I have no way to tell whether the agent regressed or the task image, a pip resolution, or a live website moved underneath the benchmark.
symptom: A results file holds task ids, pass flags and wall time, and nothing about the environment that produced them - no image digest, no dependency lock hash, no harness commit, no network policy. Re-running the same suite next month gives a different number and no field in either record can say why, so agent-to-agent and paper-to-paper comparisons quietly compare different experiments.
why_now: Traditional benchmarks shipped a fixed dataset, so the artifact WAS the environment. An agentic benchmark ships a container, a tool set and often a live network dependency, all of which drift on their own schedule, yet the result record is still just a score per task. 2025 guidance explicitly asks for the environment to be frozen at release and for tool versions to be stated, and finds real benchmarks failing both.
existing: Committing a Dockerfile pins the recipe, not the result: an unpinned base tag or an unlocked dependency install resolves differently on every build, so two runs of the same commit are two different environments.

Some benchmarks pin package versions in the task repository, which the ABC assessment credits, but the pin lives in the benchmark rather than in the emitted result, so a published number still cannot be traced to the environment that produced it.

Leaderboards record the model and the scaffold, sometimes the date, but not a machine-checkable environment identity, so leaderboard rows from different months are compared as if they were one experiment.

evidence.title: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
evidence.quote: Finally, the environment setup should be fully reproducible and frozen at the time of benchmark release
evidence.note: Checklist item T.6, whose next sentence advises against relying on dynamic resources such as continually updated external websites. The primitive being asked for is a frozen, identifiable environment; a result row with no environment identity cannot even show whether that requirement held for the run that produced it.

evidence.title: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
evidence.quote: For self-hosted tools, it is essential to explicitly specify the correct tool or package versions in the prompt
evidence.note: Checklist item T.1. Tool and package version identity is treated as a validity condition rather than hygiene, and the per-benchmark assessment marks real benchmarks down for omitting it.

evidence.title: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
evidence.quote: The prompt does not specify the versions of important tools, such as Python and Pytorch.
evidence.note: The per-benchmark assessment table scoring a widely used agentic benchmark 0 on that item, which is direct evidence the omission is the norm rather than a hypothetical.

evidence.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
evidence.quote: Before starting tasks, developers forecast that allowing AI will reduce completion time by 24%.
evidence.note: Establishes the size of the belief-to-measurement gap this record is about closing: expectations formed off benchmark-era evidence were wrong in sign on real tasks, so the environment a score was measured in is load-bearing information.

build_hypothesis: An env_fingerprint() the harness calls once per run and stamps into every result row - image digest, dependency lockfile hash, harness commit, model and scaffold identity, network policy - plus a compare command that refuses to diff two result sets whose fingerprints differ without saying which fields moved. The value is not the hash, it is that a score becomes a measurement with its conditions attached rather than a number.

check.manual_question: Open the newest result file your eval suite wrote. Which fields in a single row let a stranger rebuild the exact environment that produced it - image digest, dependency lock hash, harness commit, network policy - and if none do, what evidence do you have that last month's number was measured under the same conditions?
check.rationale: The signature is a project that emits per-task scores while no file anywhere names an environment identity primitive, which is the measurable form of a score with no conditions attached. What it can get wrong: a project may pin its environment somewhere this vocabulary does not cover (a Nix flake, a Bazel lock, an internal build id), which reads as PRESENT when the practice is actually in place, so a hit is a prompt to look rather than a conviction; conversely the mitigation rule credits the mere presence of a digest or lock anywhere in the tree, which is weaker than proving it is stamped into the result row.

bad.Dockerfile:
FROM python:latest
RUN pip install requests pytest playwright
COPY harness /harness

good.harness/report.py:
"""Write benchmark result rows, each pinned to the environment that produced it."""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess


def env_fingerprint():
    """Everything a reader needs to reproduce this row a year from now."""
    return {
        "image_digest": os.environ["EVAL_IMAGE_DIGEST"],
        "lockfile_sha256": hashlib.sha256(open("uv.lock", "rb").read()).hexdigest(),
        "harness_commit": subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"]).decode().strip(),
        "network": os.environ.get("EVAL_NETWORK_POLICY", "denied"),
    }


def write_result(task_id, passed, wall_seconds):
    row = {"task_id": task_id, "passed": passed, "wall_seconds": wall_seconds,
           "env_fingerprint": env_fingerprint()}
    with open("results.jsonl", "a") as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
